messages:
casey: Heads-up - onboarding sample shows inconsistent error ergonomics across SDKs when handling auth + rate-limit responses.
meera: example?
casey: TS SDK throws '401' string or '429 Too Many Requests' string from fetch; Python & Go expose typed errors with fields like .Type and .Retryable. New users copy the TS sample and end up with brittle string checks.
dave: ouch. We should define a minimal, flat error contract clients can rely on: type, status, retryable, hint, raw. Keep values primitives only.
meera: Agree. Suggest 'type' values like 'Auth.RefreshNeeded' or 'Rate.Limited' and hint strings like 'refresh_token' or 'wait:60'.
casey: Also include a stable 'retry_after' number if server sends it, but don't force it - keep optional.
dave: Ops question: do we map 429 to retryable=true always? Some 429s are client misbehavior vs transient burst.
meera: We can add subcodes: 'rate.burst' vs 'rate.daily', and SDKs default to retryable for burst but not daily quota.
casey: Actionables: 1) spec PR in DEVEX repo with canonical fields + examples in TS/Go/Python, 2) quickstart sample patch to demonstrate detection + friendly logs, 3) SDK adapter to normalize fetch/errors into the contract behind a feature flag.
sdk-bot: Created DEVEX-6120: "SDK error ergonomics: canonical client error shape + quickstart updates" https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/6120
meera: I'll draft the spec and sample snippets. dave: I'll take TS adapter + tests. casey: i'll update onboarding sample app and add an e2e for expired key and a simulated 429.
casey: thanks everyone, aiming to have drafts by EOW. :thumbsup:
